A father of two has been killed while working as a food delivery rider in Melbourne’s CBD, after he and another rider were allegedly stabbed by a man they caught tampering with their bikes.

Police were called to the Chongqing Chicken Pot City restaurant in Frederick Way, near the Queen Victoria Market, shortly after 8pm on Friday and found a man with stab wounds. CPR was performed, but the man – a registered HungryPanda food delivery rider – was declared dead at the scene.

A short time later, a second man, aged 34, was found nearby with a suspected stab wound and was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

Detectives believe the two riders confronted a man they caught tampering with their bikes and an altercation broke out.

A 51-year-old Footscray man was arrested in Footscray on Saturday morning. He remains in custody and is expected to be interviewed by police.

Police established two crime scenes about 100 metres apart, and major roads were closed in an area of the city that is home to a large community of Chinese students and tourists.

University student Zeikei Shou, who lives nearby, said that on Friday night, he heard the commotion before arriving to what he described as “chaos”.

Shou said he saw a man running from the scene with a knife.

“Another two delivery guys tried to stop him but one of them fell, and then he was stabbed. He is now in hospital,” he said.

Shou said he was devastated both victims were from China, and called for greater protection for delivery riders, who he said were frequently harassed and assaulted in the CBD.

“One man lost his life, he is a father of two. He has delivered food to me before, I know his face,” he said.

“He is here on a working holiday visa, working really hard. He works really hard every day, delivering food for 10 to 12 hours a day.”

Shou said he believed the victim’s family were travelling from China and expected to arrive in Melbourne on Saturday night.
